target_customer: Credit unions and community banks buying digital banking software
problem: Credit unions had clunky mobile and online banking from legacy vendors compared with modern consumer apps.
business_model: B2B SaaS licensing to financial institutions

founders.name: Mike Duncan
founders.background_notes: Programmer at a Michigan credit union before founding Bankjoy in Jan 2015.

competitors.name: Legacy credit union core and digital banking vendors
competitors.what: Large banking software vendors criticized by the article

technical_complexity.rationale: Needs integrations with credit union core systems and security compliance, standard but heavy.

defensibility.rationale: Core integration and long credit union contracts create lock-in, but sales cycles are slow.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents were not reported to copy it; Bankjoy grew to about 60 to 68 institutions by 2023.

market_need_then: About 6,000 US credit unions serving nearly 100 million members, and about 100 credit unions said they would demo it at launch per TechCrunch in March 2015.

identity.voice_and_tone: Friendly joyful word, credit union focused

brand_strength.rationale: No brand-specific coverage. The name joy fits the pitch but there is no evidence it drove growth.

outcome_analysis: Bankjoy is a slow compounding B2B company. A founder who came from credit union software sold to credit unions from 2015, grew to about 60 clients by 2023 with 1 million members reached, and took a strategic round from Curql Collective and client credit unions in March 2023. It has not reported a venture scale outcome, but it is active, with about 60 staff.
notes: Finovate reports $1.8M raised earlier from SixThirty and CheckAlt, undated, single outlet, so not recorded as a round. 2023 amount undisclosed. Bessemer is named as an investor in secondary sources without round details.
